A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same f-DP analysis of Noisy-FedAvg and Noisy-FedProx. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The earlier proofs largely map to v3 Appendix G, while several preliminary sections move to other appendices.

before.justification: V2 reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 accuracy experiments and sensitivity studies in Section 5, Tables 6–7, and Figure 2.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results in Section 5 and adds original benchmark, sensitivity, and privacy-attack results in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the Noisy-FedAvg and Noisy-FedProx updates in Eqs. (2)–(4) retain the same clipping, proximal regularization, client-side Gaussian perturbation, and aggregation procedures. The additional architectures and learning-rate experiments evaluate the existing methods.

E1.justification: V3 adds CIFAR-100 and TinyImagenet to the retained MNIST/CIFAR-10 coverage. Appendices C–D also introduce client identification labeled membership inference, label reconstruction, image reconstruction through gradient inversion, attribute inference, and surrogate-model extraction, substantially expanding the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: The evaluated Noisy-FedAvg versus Noisy-FedProx comparison retains the same methods and proximal-coefficient variants in v2 Table 7 and v3 Table 5. New architecture comparisons, noise-free controls, and attack scenarios do not introduce an additional competing FL algorithm.

E3.justification: The retained accuracy comparison keeps its client counts, local intervals, and TK = 30000 budget. Added experiments introduce client counts of 20 and 500, K = 500, ViT-Small evaluation through T = 1000, four learning-rate schedules, and attack evaluations with 500 or 1000 samples and zero-noise controls. These are additional protocols, not demonstrated changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: V2's sensitivity sweeps over client count, local interval, clipping, and proximal regularization remain. V3 adds architecture-dependent stability comparisons, empirical tests of all four learning-rate schedules, local-sample-count sensitivity, and resistance to several attacks under constant noise. These investigate substantial additional robustness and mechanism questions.

E5.justification: The original accuracy table retains the statement that results are repeated five times to report mean and variance, with identical uncertainty entries. V3 Table 8 extends the existing plus/minus presentation, while other new tables report point values. No new seed policy, confidence interval, significance test, or explicit increase in repeated runs is reported.

E6.justification: The original accuracy and FedAvg/FedProx sensitivity results are unchanged, but v3 Tables 7–16 add substantial results. For example, Table 9 reports T = 600 sensitivities of 37.98 for constant and 24.68 for iterative decay. Table 11 reports T = 1000 attack success of 30%, 70%, and 100% for noise levels 0.1, 0.01, and zero. These are newly reported comparisons, not gains over v2 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The principal privacy bounds and most derivations remain. V3 adds a Gaussian-coupling argument and a GDP accumulation lemma with proof in Appendix E, plus partial-participation reasoning in Remark 3.2. Appendix G.3 corrects the erroneous gamma_t coefficient in v2 Eq. (39) to rho_t, but omits the explicit Cauchy–Schwarz equality condition previously given in Eq. (41).

C1.justification: V3 qualifies the introduction's priority claim as the first convergent FL-DP privacy analysis for non-convex functions, whereas v2 states priority for FL-DP methods generally. The central convergence, proximal-regularization, and DP-conversion claims remain. The conclusion additionally foregrounds empirical validation.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly focuses its threat discussion on global-model privacy, adds applicability and relaxation-tightness arguments, and interprets the new architecture, sample-count, and attack studies. V2's dedicated online-learning-rate caveat in Corollary 14 is omitted. Some new interpretation conflicts with the evidence: Appendix C says eventual ViT sensitivity does not exceed ResNet-18, although Table 7 reports 36.58 versus 24.17.

D1.justification: V3 newly identifies stage-wise learning-rate decay for the retained experiments; this is disclosure rather than evidence of a changed procedure. Appendices C–D provide additional attacker inputs and evaluation sample counts. Conversely, v2's explicit sentence describing construction of adjacent CIFAR-10 datasets for the sensitivity study is omitted.

R1.justification: The central positioning against previous FL-DP privacy analyses remains. V3 adds Arevalo et al. (2024) and several FL references, while removing references including Bun's concentrated-DP works, Hardt et al. (2016), and Li et al. (2020). Appendix F adds a more explicit comparison with the bounded-domain assumptions attributed to Bok et al. (2024).

P1.justification: The introduction and main theoretical exposition are extensively condensed and rewritten. Related work moves before the preliminaries; notation, pseudocode, and standard f-DP properties move into separate appendices, and the proofs become Appendix G. The title, author information, section headings, and conference header also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 becomes a two-panel illustration adding the global interpolation path and redrawing the sensitivity decomposition. The notation table is expanded and relocated, v2's qualitative Table 5 is removed, and ten experimental tables are added. Existing tables are resized and rearranged within a substantially reformatted conference layout; Figures 2–3 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V3's learning-rate and attack studies address relevant empirical questions, while the expanded Figure 1 and GDP proof help explain the analysis. However, the ViT interpretation contradicts Table 7, and the membership-inference protocol describes 500 steps while Table 11 extends to T = 1000. Appendix F also asserts NP-hardness and negligible relaxation gaps without a derivation. These unresolved weaknesses in the added evidence and justification prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the broader coverage.
